w001.def: Very large in amount; more than plenty.
w001.ex1: After copious spring rain, the pond filled with frogs for the water snakes to hunt.
w001.ex2: She took copious notes during the lecture.

w002.def: Thinly scattered; few and far apart.
w002.ex1: In the desert, plants are sparse, so lizards must travel far to find shade.
w002.ex2: The old man's hair had grown sparse.

w003.ex1: A large tank gives a growing snake ample room to stretch out.
w003.ex2: We had ample time to finish before dinner.

w004.def: Very small in amount; barely enough.
w004.ex1: A single cricket is a meager meal for a full-grown bearded dragon.
w004.ex2: He saved his meager allowance for three months to buy the book.

w005.def: An amount left over beyond what is needed.
w005.ex1: The zoo shared its surplus of feeder mice with the reptile rescue.
w005.ex2: The bake sale ended with a surplus of cookies.

w006.ex1: Titanoboa was a colossal prehistoric snake, as long as a school bus.
w006.ex2: Building the bridge was a colossal project.

w007.ex1: The thread snake is so minute it can be mistaken for an earthworm.
w007.ex2: She checked the map for even the most minute details.

w008.ex1: Komodo dragons roam an expansive territory in search of food.
w008.ex2: The hotel room had an expansive view of the bay.

w009.def: So small that it does not matter.
w009.ex1: The bite of a baby garter snake does a negligible amount of harm.
w009.ex2: The difference in price was negligible.

w010.def: Large in amount, size, or importance.
w010.ex1: After a substantial meal, a boa may not eat again for weeks.
w010.ex2: He made a substantial improvement in his handwriting this year.

w011.ex1: On a warm morning the racer snake moves at a brisk pace through the grass.
w011.ex2: We took a brisk walk before breakfast.

w012.ex1: A snake kept too cold becomes lethargic and stops eating.
w012.ex2: The heat made everyone feel lethargic.

w013.def: To hurry; to make something happen sooner.
w013.ex1: Warm weather can hasten the hatching of turtle eggs.
w013.ex2: We hastened to finish our chores before the guests arrived.

w014.def: To stay longer than needed; to be slow to leave.
w014.ex1: A lizard will linger on a warm rock long after sunrise.
w014.ex2: The smell of popcorn lingered in the kitchen.

w015.ex1: An abrupt movement can startle a resting snake.
w015.ex2: The bus came to an abrupt stop.

w016.def: To state something firmly and with confidence.
w016.ex1: Some keepers assert that their snakes recognize them.
w016.ex2: She asserted that the answer in the book was wrong.

w017.ex1: Visitors often inquire about which snakes are venomous.
w017.ex2: He called the library to inquire about its hours.

w018.def: To explain with more detail; also, having many carefully made parts.
w018.ex1: The guide elaborated on how a rattlesnake's rattle adds a new segment with each shed.
w018.ex2: They planned an elaborate surprise party.

w019.def: To answer back quickly in a sharp or clever way.
w019.ex1: "Snakes aren't slimy at all," she retorted.
w019.ex2: His quick retort made the whole table laugh.

w020.def: To announce something publicly and proudly.
w020.ex1: The sign proclaimed the arrival of a rare king cobra at the zoo.
w020.ex2: The mayor proclaimed Saturday a town holiday.

w021.def: To think about something deeply and for a long time.
w021.ex1: He contemplated for weeks whether a bearded dragon or a gecko would suit him better.
w021.ex2: She contemplated the painting in silence.

w022.def: To guess about something without having all the facts.
w022.ex1: Some scientists speculate that the earliest snakes lived underground.
w022.ex2: We can only speculate about who left the note.

w023.def: To figure something out from clues instead of being told.
w023.ex1: From the shed skin, we can infer that the snake is growing.
w023.ex2: From her muddy boots, I inferred she had been in the garden.

w024.def: To reach an answer by reasoning from the facts you have.
w024.ex1: From the shape of its head and its pattern, she deduced which species it was.
w024.ex2: The detective deduced that the thief was left-handed.

w025.def: To remember something, often with effort.
w025.ex1: The old keeper could recollect every snake he had ever cared for.
w025.ex2: I cannot recollect where we parked.

w026.def: Extremely bold and daring, even shocking.
w026.ex1: The audacious roadrunner will attack a rattlesnake.
w026.ex2: It was an audacious plan to cross the ocean in a rowboat.

w027.def: Worried that something bad may happen.
w027.ex1: She felt apprehensive the first time she held a python.
w027.ex2: He was apprehensive about his first day at the new co-op.

w028.def: Very brave, especially when things are hard.
w028.ex1: The mother bird made a valiant effort to drive the snake from her nest.
w028.ex2: The team lost, but it was a valiant try.

w029.def: Seeming so hard or frightening that it discourages you.
w029.ex1: Cleaning a twelve-foot python's enclosure is a daunting job.
w029.ex2: The thousand-piece puzzle looked daunting at first.

w030.def: Not willing; slow to do something because you don't want to.
w030.ex1: A newly arrived snake is often reluctant to eat for the first week.
w030.ex2: He was reluctant to jump into the cold pool.

w031.ex1: He was elated when his gecko's eggs finally hatched.
w031.ex2: She was elated to win first place.

w032.ex1: The turtle basked on a log in the serene morning light.
w032.ex2: The lake was serene at sunrise.

w033.def: Sad in a quiet, thoughtful way; a quiet sadness.
w033.ex1: He felt melancholy for days after his old gecko died.
w033.ex2: The slow song had a melancholy sound.

w034.def: Upset, nervous, and unable to stay calm.
w034.ex1: An agitated rattlesnake shakes its tail as a warning.

w035.ex1: Snakes are often irritable while shedding because they cannot see well.

w036.ex1: She gave a sincere apology for leaving the terrarium lid open.
w036.ex2: His thank-you note was short but sincere.

w037.def: Firm and unchanging in loyalty or purpose.
w037.ex1: She was steadfast in caring for the rescued tortoise, never missing a day.
w037.ex2: He remained a steadfast friend through hard times.

w038.def: Kind and eager to do good for others.
w038.ex1: A benevolent neighbor donated tanks to the reptile rescue.
w038.ex2: The benevolent king lowered the taxes.

w039.def: Not bragging; not thinking you are better than others.
w039.ex1: The famous snake expert stayed humble and answered every child's question.
w039.ex2: She was humble about winning and praised the other team.

w040.ex1: A diligent keeper checks the tank's temperature every day.
w040.ex2: Diligent practice made him a better pianist.

w041.def: Acting as if you are better or more important than others.
w041.ex1: The arrogant hiker ignored the rattlesnake warning signs.

w042.def: Stubbornly refusing to change, no matter what.
w042.ex1: The obstinate tortoise pushed against the fence all afternoon.
w042.ex2: He was too obstinate to admit his mistake.

w043.def: Dishonest; tricking people by hiding the truth.
w043.ex1: In the fable, the deceitful snake tricks the trusting frog.

w044.def: Hating to spend or share money; stingy.
w044.ex1: The miserly owner refused to buy a proper heat lamp for his lizard.
w044.ex2: The miserly man kept his fortune hidden under the floor.

w045.ex1: A well-fed crocodile looks indolent, but it can move in a flash.
w045.ex2: The indolent student left everything until the last minute.

w046.ex1: New fossil finds bolster the idea that snakes evolved from lizards.
w046.ex2: A good breakfast will bolster your energy for the test.

w047.def: To make something harder to do; to slow down.
w047.ex1: Cold weather will hinder a snake's ability to digest its food.
w047.ex2: Heavy traffic hindered our trip to the airport.

w048.def: To keep safe from harm; to keep something the way it is.
w048.ex1: The park was created to preserve the home of the gopher tortoise.
w048.ex2: We preserve peaches in jars every summer.

w049.ex1: Bulldozers demolished the old barn where the rat snakes had lived.
w049.ex2: The hungry team demolished three pizzas.

w050.def: To weaken something slowly or secretly.
w050.ex1: Draining the marsh would undermine years of work to protect the turtles.
w050.ex2: Constant teasing can undermine a person's confidence.

w051.def: To change something slightly, usually to improve it.
w051.ex1: Keepers modify the tank's temperature as the seasons change.
w051.ex2: We modified the recipe to make it dairy-free.

w052.def: To make louder, larger, or stronger.
w052.ex1: A hollow log can amplify the sound of a rattlesnake's warning.

w053.def: To slowly become smaller or fewer.
w053.ex1: As the wetlands dry up, the number of water snakes will dwindle.
w053.ex2: Our supply of firewood dwindled as the night went on.

w054.def: To change and develop slowly over time.
w054.ex1: Snakes evolved from lizard ancestors over millions of years.
w054.ex2: His sketches evolved into a full comic book.

w055.def: To bring something back to the way it was.
w055.ex1: Volunteers worked to restore the marsh where the turtles nest.
w055.ex2: He restored the rusty bike until it looked new.

w056.ex1: The snakes' long winter rest will commence when the nights turn cold.
w056.ex2: The ceremony will commence at noon.

w057.ex1: When the rattling ceased, the hikers knew the snake had moved on.
w057.ex2: The rain ceased just before the game.

w058.def: To begin again after a pause.
w058.ex1: After shedding, the snake will resume eating.

w059.def: To stop for a while; also, to hang from above.
w059.ex1: The zoo had to suspend its snake-handling shows during the heat wave.
w059.ex2: The game was suspended because of lightning.

w060.def: To keep trying in spite of difficulty.
w060.ex1: A hatchling sea turtle must persevere across the beach to reach the waves.
w060.ex2: She persevered until she solved the last problem.

w061.def: Easy to see or understand; clear.
w061.ex1: It was evident from its cloudy eyes that the snake was about to shed.
w061.ex2: Her relief was evident to everyone.

w062.ex1: He gave only a vague description of the snake he saw.
w062.ex2: I have a vague memory of that vacation.

w063.ex1: A striking snake needs precise aim to catch a moving mouse.

w064.def: Able to be understood in more than one way; unclear.
w064.ex1: The label "green snake" is ambiguous, because many species are green.
w064.ex2: His ambiguous answer left us wondering what he meant.

w065.def: Not well known or hard to see; also, to hide from view.
w065.ex1: Fallen leaves obscure the copperhead so well that hikers walk right past it.
w065.ex2: The answer was in an obscure old book.

w066.def: Very old and no longer in common use.
w066.ex1: The museum displayed archaic remedies once used for snakebites.

w067.def: Belonging to the present time; also, living at the same time.
w067.ex1: Contemporary zoos build habitats that copy a reptile's wild home.

w068.ex1: Researchers used an innovative tiny radio tag to follow the snakes.
w068.ex2: The company is known for its innovative designs.

w069.def: An old and valuable object; old and valuable.
w069.ex1: The museum displayed an antique bracelet shaped like a coiled snake.
w069.ex2: Grandma's antique clock still keeps perfect time.

w070.def: No longer used because something newer has replaced it.
w070.ex1: Old snakebite kits are now obsolete; doctors use antivenom instead.
w070.ex2: Smartphones made many paper maps obsolete.

w071.def: Real and true; not a copy.
w071.ex1: The fossil was tested and proved to be an authentic dinosaur egg.
w071.ex2: The restaurant serves authentic Mexican food.

w072.def: Made to look real in order to fool people; a fake.
w072.ex1: The "snakeskin" belt turned out to be counterfeit plastic.
w072.ex2: The cashier spotted the counterfeit bill.

w073.def: To make someone believe something that is not true.
w073.ex1: The harmless milk snake's colors deceive predators into thinking it is a coral snake.
w073.ex2: The magician deceived the audience with a hidden card.

w074.ex1: Its sandy color helps conceal the horned viper in the desert.
w074.ex2: She concealed the gift behind her back.

w075.def: To tell something that was secret.
w075.ex1: The researcher would not divulge where the rare turtles nest, to keep them safe.
w075.ex2: He refused to divulge the surprise ending.

w076.ex1: His parents consented to a pet snake once he proved he could care for it.
w076.ex2: You need a parent's consent for the field trip.

w077.def: To say the opposite; to disagree with.
w077.ex1: New evidence may contradict the old belief that snakes are deaf.
w077.ex2: The two witnesses contradicted each other.

w078.def: An argument or disagreement; to argue about something.
w078.ex1: Scientists dispute how many kinds of python really exist.
w078.ex2: The umpire settled the dispute at home plate.

w079.def: To admit that something is true, often unwillingly; also, to give up.
w079.ex1: He had to concede that the harmless snake was helping the garden.
w079.ex2: She conceded the chess match after losing her queen.

w080.def: An agreement where each side gives up something.
w080.ex1: As a compromise, he got a small corn snake instead of a giant python.
w080.ex2: We reached a compromise about whose turn it was.

w081.ex1: A robust corn snake eats well and sheds in one piece.
w081.ex2: The table is robust enough to stand on.

w082.def: Hard but easily broken or snapped.
w082.ex1: An old shed snakeskin becomes dry and brittle.
w082.ex2: The dry twigs were brittle and snapped underfoot.

w083.ex1: The sick hatchling was too feeble to eat on its own.
w083.ex2: He gave a feeble excuse for being late.

w084.def: Stiff and not bending; also, very strict.
w084.ex1: A turtle's shell is rigid, but a snake's body bends in every direction.
w084.ex2: The camp has rigid rules about bedtime.

w085.def: Able to recover quickly after difficulty.
w085.ex1: Geckos are resilient: many can regrow a lost tail.
w085.ex2: Children are often more resilient than adults expect.

w086.def: The surface features of an area of land.
w086.ex1: Sidewinders are built for sandy terrain.
w086.ex2: The rocky terrain slowed the hikers down.

w087.def: The outer edge or boundary of an area.
w087.ex1: The keeper walked the perimeter of the enclosure, checking for gaps.
w087.ex2: A fence runs around the perimeter of the playground.

w088.def: The highest point of a mountain.
w088.ex1: Few reptiles can survive the cold near a mountain summit.
w088.ex2: We reached the summit just before sunset.

w089.ex1: Signs warned that rattlesnakes had been seen in the vicinity.
w089.ex2: There are three parks in the vicinity of our house.

w090.def: The edge of settled land; the limit of what is known.
w090.ex1: Settlers on the frontier learned to check their boots for snakes.
w090.ex2: The deep ocean is one of the last frontiers on Earth.

w091.def: A person or animal that comes from an ancestor.
w091.ex1: Birds are the living descendants of dinosaurs.
w091.ex2: She is a descendant of the town's founder.

w092.def: Someone you know a little, but who is not a close friend.
w092.ex1: An acquaintance from the reptile club offered him a spare tank.
w092.ex2: He is more of an acquaintance than a friend.

w093.ex1: The mongoose is the cobra's most famous adversary.
w093.ex2: She shook hands with her adversary after the match.

w094.ex1: A corn snake is a good pet for a novice because it is gentle and hardy.
w094.ex2: Even a novice can learn this card game quickly.

w095.def: A person who watches an event.
w095.ex1: Spectators gasped as the keeper lifted the giant anaconda.
w095.ex2: The spectators cheered at the finish line.

w096.ex1: Zoos strive to give every reptile a home like its wild one.
w096.ex2: Always strive to do your best work.

w097.def: To reach or achieve after effort.
w097.ex1: Few snakes in the wild attain their full possible length.
w097.ex2: She attained her goal of reading forty books.

w098.def: To try hard; a serious effort.
w098.ex1: The team will endeavor to return every rescued turtle to the sea.
w098.ex2: Learning German has been a rewarding endeavor.

w099.def: To work very hard for a long time; long, hard work.
w099.ex1: Workers toiled all summer to build the new reptile house.
w099.ex2: After hours of toil, the garden was finally planted.

w100.def: To win in the end; to prove stronger.
w100.ex1: In a fight between two king snakes, the larger usually prevails.
w100.ex2: Common sense prevailed, and the trip was postponed.

w101.ex1: Busy roads are a serious hazard for turtles crossing to lay their eggs.
w101.ex2: Toys on the stairs are a safety hazard.

w102.ex1: A snake out in the open is in peril from hawks overhead.
w102.ex2: The sailors faced great peril during the storm.

w103.ex1: A basking lizard stays vigilant, ready to dash at any shadow.
w103.ex2: Lifeguards must remain vigilant all day.

w104.def: To make stronger or safer against attack.
w104.ex1: They had to fortify the tortoise pen after a raccoon dug under it.
w104.ex2: The soldiers fortified the walls of the castle.

w105.ex1: A snake is most vulnerable right after a big meal, when it cannot move fast.
w105.ex2: Without a coat, you are vulnerable to the cold.

w106.def: A quick look at only part of something.
w106.ex1: We caught only a glimpse of the snake's tail as it slid under the rock.
w106.ex2: I glimpsed the ocean between the buildings.

w107.ex1: One glance at the rattle told her to back away.
w107.ex2: He glanced at the clock and kept working.

w108.def: To look steadily for a long time.
w108.ex1: Snakes have no eyelids, so they seem to gaze without ever blinking.
w108.ex2: We gazed at the stars from the backyard.

w109.def: To examine very carefully, looking at every detail.
w109.ex1: The vet scrutinized each scale for signs of infection.
w109.ex2: The teacher scrutinized the essay for errors.

w110.def: To look over the whole of something; also, a broad study.
w110.ex1: From its branch, the tree boa can survey the forest floor below.
w110.ex2: We paused at the top to survey the valley.

w111.def: So necessary that you cannot do without it.
w111.ex1: A reliable thermometer is indispensable for keeping reptiles.
w111.ex2: A good map is indispensable on a long hike.

w112.def: Extremely important, especially to how something turns out.
w112.ex1: Getting antivenom quickly is crucial after a venomous bite.
w112.ex2: The last inning was crucial to the game.

w113.def: Important or large enough to notice.
w113.ex1: Snakes play a significant role in controlling rats and mice.
w113.ex2: There was a significant change in the weather overnight.

w114.ex1: Moving the lamp made only a marginal difference in the tank's temperature.
w114.ex2: The new rule had only a marginal effect.

w115.ex1: The difference between the two lizards seemed trivial, but it proved they were separate species.

w116.ex1: Even mundane chores, like changing the water, keep a reptile healthy.
w116.ex2: Washing dishes is a mundane task.

w117.def: Following the usual, accepted way of doing things.
w117.ex1: Instead of a conventional glass tank, he built a wooden enclosure.
w117.ex2: She chose a conventional design for the invitation.

w118.ex1: The hognose snake has a peculiar habit of playing dead.
w118.ex2: There was a peculiar noise coming from the attic.

w119.def: Having a special quality that makes it easy to recognize.
w119.ex1: The rattlesnake's distinctive buzz is a sound hikers never forget.
w119.ex2: The bakery has a distinctive smell of cinnamon.

w120.def: Much better or more unusual than normal.
w120.ex1: A two-headed snake is an exceptional find.
w120.ex2: Her exceptional memory amazed the class.

w121.def: A sheltered place for ships; also, to shelter, or to keep a feeling inside.
w121.ex1: A single rock pile can harbor dozens of snakes through the winter.
w121.ex2: The boats returned to the harbor before the storm.

w122.def: Very serious; also, a place where a body is buried.
w122.ex1: A cobra bite is a grave emergency.
w122.ex2: They placed flowers on the soldier's grave.

w123.def: The way a person behaves; also, to lead or carry out.
w123.ex1: Scientists conduct surveys at night to count the snakes.
w123.ex2: His conduct at the ceremony was excellent.

w124.def: A long made-up story in a book; also, new and unusual.
w124.ex1: Scientists found a novel way to track snakes using tiny radio tags.
w124.ex2: He read a whole novel on the car trip.

w125.def: A written agreement; also, to shrink or tighten.
w125.ex1: A constrictor's muscles contract each time its prey breathes out.
